spirit: Rising Heat of Stone and Sand

rules.name: BLISTERING HEAT
rules.text: At your [Sacred Site] , Invaders have -1 Health (min. 1).
rules.turn:
at P L, piece:kind P K, invader K, kind:health K H, gt H 1,
  sacred-site S L, spirit:special S blistering-heat
  / health P -1
rules.evidence: Fast '2 Damage' at Heat's Sacred Site with a Town and City: seeds 1-3 'assign *.. l3 2; assign-damage l3 0' destroying the City (Health 3-1=2); control without the rule: only the Town can be destroyed. Final health report shows the City back at 3 once the Sacred Site is gone.
rules.notes: Health is a @sum relation (bx-damage.t), so -1 is one added contribution. 'min. 1' is approximated by only applying -1 to Invaders whose printed Health is above 1; that is exact only while this is the sole Health modifier — a clamp over the sum is not additive and would need the base to expose effective-health = max(1, raw sum) as a second layer. Partial because the shared Damage model has no partial Damage carry-over.

base_ext: bx-damage.t (shared with teeth): Invader Health as `#acc health : e @sum` from kind:health; a Power's Damage as `#acc power-damage : spirit power land @sum`; Damage assignment by repeated rng choice of an Invader whose Health fits the remaining Damage (no partial Damage). Run: run.sh core.t bx-damage.t spirit-heat.t
language_issues: Recursive episodes nest (assign-damage inside assign inside assign-damage), so an outer episode is still alive during the inner step and an acc relation keyed only by land (assignable L V) mixed rows from D=2 and D=1; fix: key the acc row by every argument of the episode (assignable L D V).
Clamping a summed quantity (min. 1) cannot be expressed as another @sum contribution; needs a separate post-aggregation layer in the base.
